title: Round Revised Fuzzy Metric Spaces and Nested-Ball Fixed-Point Principles
content: Revised fuzzy metrics are distance-like structures defined using continuous triangular conorms. Although their induced topologies possess several metric-type properties, the closure of an open revised fuzzy ball need not coincide with the corresponding closed ball. We introduce round revised fuzzy metric spaces as those for which this equality holds. A two-point counterexample disproves the equality in general, while the inclusion of the closure of every open ball in the corresponding closed ball is established. We examine the behaviour of roundness under isometries, subspaces and finite products, and show that roundness of the standard revised fuzzy metric induced by a metric is equivalent to classical metric roundness. We also establish a Cantor-type characterization of completeness through decreasing sequences of nonempty closed sets with vanishing revised fuzzy diameter. In complete round spaces, this characterization yields a nested-ball fixed-point principle for continuous self-maps that send each open ball into its successor. The method is local, requires no prescribed global contractive inequality, and is illustrated by metric, linear and nonlinear examples.
